question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹1,200 at an interest rate of 3% per month in 1 month.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 1 month is simply the **percentage of the principal** for that period.

**Simple Interest (SI)** = 3% of ₹1,200

SI = (3 ÷ 100) × 1,200

SI = 3 × 12 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is ₹36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,200

**Rate of interest (R)** = 3% per month

**Time (T)** = 1 month

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/257986dbd54772c286bb99a17eabf087b5e53e655a7c8fd843dea85de5b8e032.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (1,200 × 3 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (3,600) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 36

**∴ The correct answer is ₹36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after interest is the sum of the principal and simple interest: A = P + SI.

Annual vs Monthly Rate

If the rate is given annually and time in months, divide the annual rate by 12 or convert time to years (T/12).

Simple Interest Nature

Simple interest remains **constant** for every equal time period as it is always calculated on the original principal.
